comment: K1077 supplied the decisive scoped preference: at T256 on difficult 2–3-turn spirals, high-rate RMSprop smooth networks can beat rectifier candidates despite fewer LayerNorms. B fits that regime; C’s residual connections and terminal normalization did not overturn it. K1002 and K1012 helped exclude A: its Adagrad displacement is only about 0.00096, indicating severe undertraining. K1078 appropriately limits confidence in an activation-only explanation, since normalization and architecture can change the smooth-versus-rectifier ordering. This result supports the existing recipe-level preference, not a new universal maximum-rate or GELU rule.
